description:
Find and fix supported accessibility issues on your WordPress site: image alt text, headings and link text. Every fix is previewed and can be undone.

Ask for an accessibility check and WP Accessibility Fixer reads your posts and pages for common problems: images without alt text, skipped heading levels, vague link text such as "click here", form fields without labels and low text contrast, plus the homepage's language, title, main area and skip link. The report says which problems can be fixed in your content and which belong to your theme, a plugin or a page builder.

Your assistant writes the alt text and link text. WP Accessibility Fixer shows a preview, saves only when you confirm, and can undo any change later. Automated checks find only some accessibility problems; a full review needs manual testing.

Connect your self-hosted WordPress site with a one-time approval link in your wp-admin: no password is shared and no plugin is required. WP Accessibility Fixer is made by the WP Image Fixer team.

positive.description: Check the site for accessibility problems
positive.prompt: Use WP Accessibility Fixer to check my WordPress site for accessibility problems.
positive.expected_behavior: A summary by problem type, split into "can be fixed in your content" (images without alt text, a skipped heading, a "click here" link, links that show a bare web address) and "reported only" with who can fix each (the theme, a plugin or the editor), ending with: "Automated checks find only some accessibility problems; a full review needs manual testing." Nothing changes.

positive.description: Show the details behind one problem
positive.prompt: Use WP Accessibility Fixer to show me which pages have vague link text.
positive.expected_behavior: The demo page https://www.aiwordpressguide.com/accessibility-demo/ is listed with its "Click here" link and the element. Nothing changes.

positive.description: Fix everything on the demo page with one preview
positive.prompt: Use WP Accessibility Fixer to fix everything it can on the Accessibility demo page. Show me one preview first.
positive.expected_behavior: A preview of every change on that page: a short description for each image without alt text (the assistant proposes one or asks what the image shows), the thin divider marked decorative, the heading h4 -> h3, and the link texts ("Click here" and the bare web address -> text naming the destination). Before anything changes, ChatGPT shows its own box asking to allow the app; it can appear twice (the preview call, then the change); choose Allow once each time. Deny leaves everything unchanged. Then only those values change; the words around them and the link addresses stay, and each result gives a batch id for undo.

positive.prompt: Use WP Accessibility Fixer to undo the link change.
positive.expected_behavior: Before anything changes, ChatGPT shows its own box asking to allow the app; it can appear twice (the preview call, then the change); choose Allow once each time. Deny leaves everything unchanged. The link texts are back as they were; the result says they were restored.

positive.prompt: Use WP Accessibility Fixer: do accessibility rules apply to websites in the European Union?
positive.expected_behavior: A short fact with a link to the official text and the date it was checked, the line "Whether it applies to a particular site depends on the organization and the site.", and "This is general information, not legal advice." Nothing changes.
